title: Steering gear test before departure: what SOLAS V/26 requires within 12 hours

scenes.label: BEFORE DEPARTURE
scenes.heading: Sailing at 0800? Test since 2000 last night
scenes.narration: Sailing at 0800? Then your steering gear must be tested after 2000 last night. Here is what that test covers.

scenes.label: THE SITUATION
scenes.heading: Bridge on the wheel, you in the steering flat
scenes.narration: You are the third engineer: the OOW on the wheel, you in the steering gear room, for the pre-departure test.

scenes.label: SOLAS V/26
scenes.heading: Within 12 hours: every unit, every position
scenes.narration: SOLAS V/26: within 12 hours before departure, test main and auxiliary gear, remote controls, each bridge steering position and emergency power.

scenes.label: WHAT YOU TEST
scenes.heading: Indicator, alarms, full movement, linkage
scenes.narration: Then compare the rudder indicator with the actual rudder, test the failure alarms, run full rudder movement, and check linkage and bridge communications.

scenes.label: REAL CASE
scenes.heading: 35 on the bridge, 30 at the rudder
scenes.narration: Bridge indicator shows 35 degrees, local scale 30? That is a defect: report it to the Chief Engineer and Master, and log the test.

scenes.label: COMMON MISTAKE
scenes.heading: Not just the centre console
scenes.narration: The common mistake: testing from the centre console only. Every bridge steering position is part of the test, wing controls included.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Every unit, every position, every alarm
scenes.narration: Every power unit, every steering position, every alarm, and the rudder itself.

factCheck.notes: SOLAS V/26.1: within 12 hours before departure the steering gear shall be checked and tested by the ship's crew. V/26.2 (where applicable): main steering gear, auxiliary steering gear, remote steering gear control systems, steering positions located on the navigation bridge, emergency power supply, rudder angle indicators in relation to the actual rudder position, remote control system power failure alarms, steering gear power unit failure alarms, automatic isolating arrangements and other automatic equipment. V/26.3: full movement of the rudder according to the required capabilities, visual inspection of the steering gear and its connecting linkage, operation of the means of communication between bridge and steering gear compartment. V/26.5: dates of checks and tests and emergency steering drills recorded (log). Ships on regular short voyages may follow the Administration's weekly alternative (V/26.1) - not mentioned. The 35 vs 30 degree discrepancy is an illustrative example; acceptance tolerance depends on class / maker / SMS, so the script only says report and record. Bridge wing positions 'where fitted'.

meta.description: What the SOLAS V/26 steering gear test before departure really covers: within 12 hours of sailing the crew tests main and auxiliary gear, remote controls, every bridge steering position, emergency power, the rudder angle indicator against the actual rudder, alarms, full rudder movement, linkage and communications. Includes a real-case indicator discrepancy and the most common testing mistake.
